earlier_scan.source_named: Kansakar, Tej R. et al. 2011. A Grammar of Baram. Linguistic Survey of Nepal (LinSuN), Tribhuvan University (cited on Glottolog bara1357; not found online).

sources.citation: Chalise, Krishna Prasad. 2022. Acoustic analysis of the Baram phonemes. Nepalese Linguistics 35: 14-23. DOI 10.3126/nl.v35i01.46555.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Segmental acoustics only (VOT, frication, formants, diphthongs; 21 consonants, 6 vowels); the words 'stress', 'accent', 'tone' do not occur anywhere in the text layer. Cites the LEDBL outputs Kansakar et al. 2011c A Grammar of Baram and 2011b dictionary as the phonemic source.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.). Linguistic Survey of India vol. III (archive.org item;ernet.dli.2015.114955).
sources.note: The archive.org text turned out to be Part III (Kuki-Chin and Burma groups): zero occurrences of Bhramu. The Part I item (LinguisticSurveyOfIndiaVolIiiPartI) exposes no text file. Not a stress source.

sources.citation: Nepalese Linguistics vols 23-34 (2008-2019), Linguistic Society of Nepal; open PDFs at Digital Himalaya (https://www.digitalhimalaya.com/collections/journals/nepling/). Baram items: Kansakar et al. 2009 'Sociolinguistic situation of the Baram language' NL 24: 69-78; Chalise 2012 (NL 27, Baram roots vs Proto-Tibeto-Burman); Chalise 2015 (NL 30, genetic affinity); Chalise 2017 (NL 32, Baram vowel acoustics).
sources.note: Every volume's text layer a full-text search for stress/accent within 60 lines of stress/accent/tone/suprasegmental: no hit. None of the Baram articles states a stress rule (NL 27 p. c. 628-881 discusses PTB rhymes and CG clusters only).

sources.citation: Chalise, Krishna Prasad. 2022. Lexical correspondences between Baram and Thami. Nepalese Linguistics 36(1). DOI 10.3126/nl.v36i1.49453.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative lexicon (Swadesh correspondences with Thami); no stress/accent/tone statement.

sources.citation: Kansakar, Tej R., Yogendra P. Yadava, Krishna P. Chalise, Balaram Prasain, Dubi N. Dhakal & Krishna Paudel. 2011. A sociolinguistic study of the Baram language. Himalayan Linguistics 10(1): 187-226. DOI 10.5070/H910123574.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey only (speakers, domains, attitudes); no phonology and no mention of stress. Reference list confirms the LEDBL corpus of descriptions: A grammar of Baram (forthcoming 2011), Baram Nepali English Dictionary (2011), Yadava/Chalise/Prasain 2005 A basic dictionary of Baram, Chalise & Prasain 2006 field report, Kansakar et al. 2009 NL 24.
